subject: Leaf temperature calculations inc a new shiny app

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Leaf temperature calculations inc a new shiny app
parts:
Dear NicheMapR users,
I've recently added functionality to the package for leaf temperature calculations.

There's a new function called 'leaf_temperature' that uses Campbell and Norman's (1998) humid operative temperature approach but solves it with a root finder rather than using their linear approximation.

And the 'ectotherm' function now has a parameter 'leaf' which implements water loss based on stomatal and boundary layer vapour conductance in series (as in the Campbell & Norman model) but with the option to change the shape of the leaf. So if you pass 'leaf = 1' to the model, it will use the new stomatal conductance inputs g_vs_ad and g_vs_ab for the adaxial and abaxial sides of the leaf, which can be a single constant value or an hourly vector that you can modify e.g. as a function of day/night, or soil water potential. If 'leaf=2' then it will open the stomata gradually when leaf temperature rises above the CT_max to maximum values set as 'g_vs_ad_max' and 'g_vs_ab_max'.

The whole setup is also now in the form of a new shiny app which should give you a sense of how it works. Note that in that app by default I've made stomatal openness follow the transpiration predicted by the Soil Plant Atmosphere Continuum model of Campbell's embedded in the microclimate model's soil moisture calcs, and I've provided input options for that part of the model under the microclimate model settings (root properties, critical water potential for stomatal closure, etc.).

I'll explain it all in more detail in a MS that I'm putting together but in the meantime, if you're interested in leaf temperatures, please have a play and let me know if you find any issues with the overall approach and app,  or think of any improvements.

All the best,
Mike
